3.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in S.T. No.321 of 2020 (State vs. Om Prakash) arising out of Case Crime No.92 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC read with Section 3/4 D.P. sentences.text: This is the second bail application of the applicant.
The first bail application was rejected by this Court vide order dated 16.02.2023 on merits.

5. No new ground has taken up by the counsel for the applicant except the fact that the trial is going on at a snail's pace and after passing the previous order, no witnesses have been examined although the witnesses of fact have already been examined.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and also taking into consideration the fact that no new ground is there for pressing the bail application, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
8. The present bail application is hereby found devoid of merits and is accordingly rejected.

9. However, it is directed that the court below may proceed with the trial and reach at the logical conclusion expeditiously, if there is no legal impediment, within a period of one year from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
(Krishan Pahal, J.) Order Date :- 19.7.2023 Ravi Kant  Om Prakash vs State Of U.P. on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86585786/
